startDateOfTheInsurance: Start date of the insurance policy
dateWhenTheLastPremium: Date when the last premium was paid
dateOnWhichTheLife: Date on which the life assured dies
dateWhenThePolicyTerm: Date when the policy term ends and benefits are payable
theAddressOfThePerson: The address of the person who owns the policy
thePersonWhoseLife: The person whose life is insured
usedForAgeCalculation: Used for age calculation and underwriting
theFinalUnpaidPremiumBefore: The final unpaid premium before policy lapses
usedInUlipsForFund: Used in ULIPs for fund value calculation
aMixOfInsurance: A mix of insurance and investment
systemForAutoDebitingPremiums: System for auto-debiting premiums from bank accounts
forDirectCreditOfClaim: For direct credit of claim/maturity to policyholder's account
usedForAutoPayment: Used for auto payment of premiums
regulatoryBodyForInsurance: Regulatory body for insurance in India
taxDeductedOnCertainPayouts: Tax deducted on certain payouts like commissions or maturity benefits
verificationProcessOfIdentity: Verification process of identity and address
usedForTaxAndFinancial: Used for tax and financial transactions
theMinimumSurrenderValue: The minimum surrender value the insurer must pay, fixed as a percentage of premiums paid
aDiscretionarySurrenderValue: A discretionary surrender value that may be higher than the GSV, based on accrued bonuses
aRiderThatWaivesFuture: A rider that waives future premiums if the policyholder is disabled or diagnosed with a critical illness
anAdditionalPayoutIfDeath: An additional payout if death occurs due to an accident
theIrdaiIssuedNumber: The IRDAI-issued number that uniquely identifies an approved insurance product
aCentralizedSystemThatStores: A centralized system that stores a customer's KYC records for reuse across financial institutions
annualBonusDeclared: Annual bonus declared as a percentage of the sum assured, added to the policy each year
aOneTimeBonusPaid: A one-time bonus paid on maturity or death, on top of accumulated reversionary bonuses
theNumberOfYearsOver: The number of years over which premiums must be paid, which may be shorter than the policy term
theTotalDurationForWhich: The total duration for which the policy remains in force
theWindowAfterAMissed: The window after a missed premium due date — typically 15 or 30 days — during which the policy stays active and the premium can still be paid without penalty
aWindowCommonly15: A window (commonly 15 or 30 days) after receiving the policy document during which the policyholder can review and return the policy for a refund if unsatisfied
aReducedSumAssured: A reduced sum assured a policy converts to if premiums stop after a minimum number of years, instead of lapsing entirely
namingAPersonToReceive: Naming a person to receive the policy proceeds on the life assured's death — the nominee acts as a trustee for the legal heirs unless also a beneficial owner
legallyTransferringTheOwnershipRights: Legally transferring the ownership rights of a policy to another person or entity, often used when a policy is pledged for a loan
anOptionalAddOnBenefit: An optional add-on benefit attached to a base policy for extra premium, such as critical illness or accidental death cover
whenAPolicyLosesIts: When a policy loses its benefits because a premium wasn't paid even after the grace period
reinstatingALapsedPolicy: Reinstating a lapsed policy by paying overdue premiums plus interest, usually within a specified revival period
inMotorInsuranceTheCurrent: In motor insurance, the current market value of the vehicle — the maximum amount payable in case of total loss or theft
aDiscountOnMotor: A discount on motor or health premium for each claim-free year, which resets if a claim is made
aHealthInsuranceClaimSettled: A health insurance claim settled directly between the insurer and a network hospital, without the policyholder paying upfront
aDefinedPeriodAfterPolicy: A defined period after policy start during which certain health conditions or claims are not covered
aSingleHealthInsuranceSum: A single health insurance sum assured shared across all covered family members, rather than a separate cover for each
